content.directions: Suppose you are asked to give advice on whether to attend college at home or abroad, write an essay to state your opinion. You are required to write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.
content.topic: Whether to attend college at home or abroad

modelEssay.title: Whether to Attend College at Home or Abroad
modelEssay.content:
Attending college is a pivotal decision in one's life. Some students opt for domestic universities, while others seek opportunities abroad. Personally, I believe that studying abroad offers more comprehensive benefits.

First and foremost, studying abroad exposes students to diverse cultures and perspectives, fostering a global mindset. This experience can broaden one's horizons and enhance intercultural communication skills, which are invaluable in today's interconnected world. Moreover, foreign universities often boast cutting-edge facilities and renowned faculty, providing students with access to state-of-the-art research and top-tier education.

In conclusion, while attending college domestically has its merits, the advantages of studying abroad are more pronounced. It not only enriches one's educational experience but also prepares individuals for the challenges of a globalized society.

structureAnalysis.paragraph1: 引入段：提出问题，表明个人倾向于留学
structureAnalysis.paragraph2: 展开段：阐述留学的好处，如文化多样性和教育资源
structureAnalysis.paragraph3: 总结段：总结留学的优势，强调对全球化社会的适应

highlights: 使用了'pivotal decision'等高级表达
运用了'First and foremost'等过渡短语，使文章结构清晰
使用了'exposes students to diverse cultures'等复杂句式
词汇丰富，如'diverse cultures', 'global mindset', 'interconnected world'

questionGroups.title: Part II Listening Comprehension
questionGroups.directions: 请听音频并回答以下问题

transcript.text: Conversation 1.
transcript.translation: 对话一。

transcript.text: Mr. Ishiguro, have you ever found one of your books at a second-hand bookstore?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 石黑先生，您曾经在二手书店里发现过自己的书吗？

transcript.text: Yes, that kind of thing is difficult. If they've got my book there, I think, well, this is an insult. Somebody didn't want to keep my book. But if it's not there, I feel it's an insult too. I think, why aren't people exchanging my book? Why isn't it in this store?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 有过，那种事让人很为难。如果店里摆着我的书，我会想，唉，这是一种侮辱，有人不想留着我的书。可如果店里没有我的书，我也觉得是一种侮辱。我会想，为什么大家不转卖我的书？为什么这家店里没有它？

transcript.text: Does being a writer require a thick skin?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 当作家是不是需要脸皮厚一点？

transcript.text: Yes. For example, my wife can be very harsh. I began working on my latest book, The Buried Giant, in 2004. But I stopped after I showed my wife a little section. She thought it was rubbish.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 是的。比如说，我妻子可以非常严厉。我从2004年开始写我最新的书《被掩埋的巨人》，但在把一小段拿给妻子看之后我就停笔了。她觉得那是垃圾。

transcript.text: Even after you won a Booker Prize?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 即便您已经拿过布克奖了吗？

transcript.text: She's not intimidated at all. And she criticizes me in exactly the same way she did when I was first unpublished and I was starting out.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 她一点也不被吓住。她批评我的方式，跟我当年还没出版、刚起步时一模一样。

transcript.text: But you would never compromise on your vision.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 但您绝不会在自己的创作理念上妥协吧。

transcript.text: No, I wouldn't ever compromise on the essential — the ideas or the themes. This isn't really what my wife is trying to criticize me about. It's always about execution.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 不会，我绝不会在最核心的东西上妥协——也就是思想或主题。我妻子真正批评的并不是这些，她针对的始终是执行和写法。

transcript.text: So why did you put your book, The Buried Giant, aside for so long? Apparently you started working on it over ten years ago.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 那您为什么把《被掩埋的巨人》搁置了这么久？据说您十多年前就开始写它了。

transcript.text: I've often stopped writing a book and left it for a few years. And by the time I come back to it, it may have changed. Usually my imagination has moved on and I can think of different contexts or a different way to do it.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我经常会中途停下一本书，把它搁置好几年。等我再回过头来写时，它可能已经变了样。通常我的想象力已经发展到别处，我能想到不同的背景设定或不同的写法。

transcript.text: What does it feel like when you finally finish a book?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 当您终于写完一本书时，那是什么感觉？

transcript.text: It's funny you ask that, because I never have this moment when I feel, ah, I've finished. I watch footballers at the end of the match, you know, the whistle goes and they've won or lost. Until then, they've been giving everything they have, and at that moment they know it's over. It's funny for an author — there's never a finishing whistle.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 你问得真有意思，因为我从来没有那种“啊，我写完了”的时刻。我看足球运动员在比赛结束时，哨声一响，他们要么赢要么输。在那之前，他们倾尽全力，而那一刻他们知道一切都结束了。对作家来说很有意思——根本没有一声终场哨。

transcript.text: Questions 1 to 4 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
transcript.translation: 问题1至4基于你刚刚听到的对话。

transcript.text: Question 1. How would the man feel if he found one of his books at a second-hand bookstore?
transcript.translation: 问题1。如果这位男士在二手书店发现自己的一本书，他会有什么感受？

transcript.translation: 问题2。这位男士的妻子如何看待他的书？

transcript.translation: 问题3。这位男士在写作时通常会怎么做？

transcript.text: Question 4. What does the man want to say by mentioning the football match?
transcript.translation: 问题4。这位男士提到足球比赛是想表达什么？

questions.questionText: How would the man feel if he found one of his books at a second-hand bookstore?

options.label: A
options.text: He would feel insulted.

options.label: B
options.text: He would feel very sad.

options.label: C
options.text: He would be embarrassed.

options.label: D

questions.analysis: 男士谈到在二手书店看到自己的书时明确说 'this is an insult'（这是一种侮辱），因为有人不想留着他的书，故选 A。B/C/D 的悲伤、尴尬、失望都未在原文出现，他用的词始终是 'insult'。
questions.keySentence: If they've got my book there, I think, well, this is an insult.

questions.questionText: What does the man's wife think of his books?

options.label: A
options.text: They are worthy of a prize.

options.label: B
options.text: They are of little value.

options.label: C
options.text: They make good reading.

options.label: D
options.text: They need improvement.

questions.analysis: 男士说把一小段拿给妻子看后她认为 'it was rubbish'（垃圾），即认为没什么价值，对应 B。A 与原文相反（妻子毫不留情，即便他得了布克奖）；C 同样相反；D 'need improvement' 是温和说法，而妻子是直接否定，'rubbish' 更对应 'little value'。
questions.keySentence: But I stopped after I showed my wife a little section. She thought it was rubbish.

questions.questionText: What does the man do when he engages in writing?

options.label: A
options.text: He seldom writes a book straight through.

options.label: B
options.text: He writes several books simultaneously.

options.label: C
options.text: He draws on his real-life experiences.

options.label: D
options.text: He often turns to his wife for help.

questions.analysis: 男士说 'I've often stopped writing a book and left it for a few years'（常常中途停下一本书搁置数年），说明他很少一气呵成写完一本书，故选 A。B 原文未提同时写多本；C 'real-life experiences' 未提及；D 妻子是批评者而非求助对象。
questions.keySentence: I've often stopped writing a book and left it for a few years.

questions.questionText: What does the man want to say by mentioning the football match?

options.label: A
options.text: Writing a book is just like watching a football match.

options.label: B
options.text: Writers actually work every bit as hard as footballers.

options.label: C
options.text: He likes watching a football match after finishing a book.

options.label: D
options.text: Unlike a football match, there is no end to writing a book.

questions.analysis: 男士用足球比赛作对比：球员有终场哨声，知道比赛结束，但 'It's funny for an author — there's never a finishing whistle'（对作家而言永远没有一声终场哨），即写书没有明确终点，故选 D。A 把比喻说反了，他强调的是不同而非相同；B 'work as hard' 不是重点；C 原文没说喜欢写完后看球。
questions.keySentence: It's funny for an author — there's never a finishing whistle.

transcript.text: Conversation 2.
transcript.translation: 对话二。

transcript.text: According to a study of race and equity in education, black athletes are dropping out of college across the country at alarming rates. With us to talk about the findings in this study is Washington Post columnist Kevin Blackstone. Good morning.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 根据一项关于教育中种族与公平的研究，全国各地的黑人运动员正以惊人的速度从大学辍学。今天来和我们谈谈这项研究发现的是《华盛顿邮报》专栏作家凯文·布莱克斯通。早上好。

transcript.text: Good morning. How are you?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 早上好。你好吗？

transcript.text: Fine, thank you. What is new that you found in this study?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 很好，谢谢。这项研究中你发现了什么新内容？

transcript.text: Well, this is Shaun Harper's study, and he points out that on major college campuses across the country, black males make up less than 3% of undergraduate enrollments. Yet, when you look at their numbers or percentages on the revenue-generating sports teams of football and basketball, they make up well into 50 to 60% of those teams. So the idea is that they are really there to be part of the revenue-generating working class of athletes on campus, and not necessarily there to be part of the educating class, as most students in other groups are.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 嗯，这是肖恩·哈珀的研究，他指出，在全国各大高校校园里，黑人男性占本科生入学人数的比例不到3%。然而，当你看他们在橄榄球和篮球这些创收运动队中的人数或比例时，他们却占到了这些球队的50%到60%。所以这意味着，他们在校园里其实是作为创收的运动员劳动阶层而存在的，而不像其他群体的大多数学生那样，是受教育阶层的一部分。

transcript.text: Compared with other groups, I think the numbers in this group at those 65 schools are something like just barely more than half of the black male athletes graduate at all.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 与其他群体相比，我想在那65所学校里，这个群体的数据大概是，仅仅只有刚刚过半的黑人男性运动员能够最终毕业。

transcript.text: Exactly. And what's really bad about this is these athletes are supposedly promised at least one thing as reward for all their blood and sweat, and that is a college degree, which can be a transformative tool in our society when you talk about upward mobility. And that's really the troubling part about this.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 完全正确。而真正糟糕的是，这些运动员据说至少被许诺了一样东西作为他们付出血汗的回报，那就是大学学位。当我们谈到向上的社会流动时，大学学位可以是社会中一种能改变命运的工具。而这正是这件事真正令人担忧的地方。

transcript.text: Well, this has been talked about so much, really, in recent years. Why hasn't it changed?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 嗯，近年来人们其实已经谈论这个问题很多了。为什么它一直没有改变呢？

transcript.text: Well, I think one of the reasons it hasn't changed is because there's really no economic pressure to change this. All of the incentive is really on winning and not losing on the field or on the court. Coaches do not necessarily have the incentive to graduate players.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 嗯，我认为它一直没有改变的原因之一，是确实没有经济上的压力去改变它。所有的激励其实都在于在球场上取胜而不是输球。教练们未必有让球员毕业的动力。

transcript.text: Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
transcript.translation: 问题5至8基于你刚才听到的对话。

transcript.text: Question 5. What are the speakers talking about?
transcript.translation: 问题5。说话者们在谈论什么？

transcript.text: Question 6. What is the new finding about black male athletes in this study?
transcript.translation: 问题6。这项研究中关于黑人男性运动员的新发现是什么？

transcript.text: Question 7. What is the graduation rate of black male athletes?
transcript.translation: 问题7。黑人男性运动员的毕业率是多少？

transcript.text: Question 8. What accounts for black athletes' failure to obtain a college degree according to the man?
transcript.translation: 问题8。根据这位男士的说法，是什么导致了黑人运动员无法获得大学学位？

questions.questionText: What are the speakers talking about?

options.label: A
options.text: Achievements of black male athletes in college.

options.label: B
options.text: Financial assistance to black athletes in college.

options.label: C
options.text: High college dropout rates among black athletes.

options.label: D

questions.analysis: 开场即点明主题：'black athletes are dropping out of college across the country at alarming rates'，整段对话围绕黑人运动员的高辍学率/低毕业率展开，故选 C。A 错在对话讲的是问题而非成就；B 财务资助从未提及；D 入学人数只是论据之一，并非整体话题。
questions.keySentence: According to a study of race and equity in education, black athletes are dropping out of college across the country at alarming rates.

questions.questionText: What is the new finding about black male athletes in this study?

options.label: A
options.text: They display great talent in every kind of game.

options.label: B
options.text: They are better at sports than at academic work.

options.label: C
options.text: They have difficulty finding money to complete their studies.

options.label: D
options.text: They make money for the college but often fail to earn a degree.

questions.analysis: 男士指出他们占创收球队的 50%-60%，是 'revenue-generating working class of athletes'，但 'just barely more than half... graduate at all'，即为学校创收却常拿不到学位，故选 D。A、B 夸大且无据；C 把'缺钱'误当作发现，原文是缺学位而非缺钱。
questions.keySentence: So the idea is that they are really there to be part of the revenue-generating working class of athletes on campus, and not necessarily there to be part of the educating class, as most students in other groups are.

questions.questionText: What is the graduation rate of black male athletes?

options.label: A
options.text: About 15%.

options.label: B
options.text: Around 40%.

options.label: C
options.text: Slightly over 50%.

options.label: D
options.text: Approximately 70%.

questions.analysis: 女主持人说 'just barely more than half of the black male athletes graduate at all'，'刚刚过半'即略高于 50%，故选 C。其余比例均与原文'just barely more than half'不符。
questions.keySentence: I think the numbers in this group at those 65 schools are something like just barely more than half of the black male athletes graduate at all.

questions.questionText: What accounts for black athletes' failure to obtain a college degree according to the man?

options.label: A
options.text: Coaches lack the incentive to graduate them.

options.label: B
options.text: College degrees do not count much to them.

options.label: C
options.text: They have little interest in academic work.

options.label: D
options.text: Schools do not deem it a serious problem.

questions.analysis: 被问及为何没有改变时，男士说 'Coaches do not necessarily have the incentive to graduate players'，因为激励全在赢球而非育人，故选 A。B、C 把责任推给运动员，与原文相反；D 学校不重视虽相关，但男士明确归因于教练缺乏让球员毕业的动力。
questions.keySentence: Coaches do not necessarily have the incentive to graduate players.

transcript.text: Passage 1.
transcript.translation: 第一篇短文。

transcript.text: America's holiday shopping season starts on Black Friday, the day after Thanksgiving.
transcript.translation: 美国的假日购物季从黑色星期五开始，也就是感恩节后的第二天。

transcript.text: It is the busiest shopping day of the year.
transcript.translation: 这是一年中最繁忙的购物日。

transcript.text: Retailers make the most money this time of year, about 20 to 30 percent of annual revenue.
transcript.translation: 零售商在一年中的这个时候赚钱最多，约占其年收入的百分之二十到三十。

transcript.text: About 136 million people will shop during the Thanksgiving holiday weekend.
transcript.translation: 约有一亿三千六百万人会在感恩节假期周末购物。

transcript.text: More and more will shop online.
transcript.translation: 越来越多的人将在网上购物。

transcript.text: In an era of instant information, shoppers can use their mobile phones to find deals.
transcript.translation: 在这个信息即时获取的时代，购物者可以用手机寻找优惠。

transcript.text: About 183.8 million people will shop on Cyber Monday, the first Monday after Thanksgiving.
transcript.translation: 约有一亿八千三百八十万人将在网络星期一购物，也就是感恩节后的第一个星期一。

transcript.text: More than half of all holiday purchases will be made online.
transcript.translation: 超过一半的假日购物将在网上完成。

transcript.text: One in five Americans will use a tablet or smartphone.
transcript.translation: 五分之一的美国人将使用平板电脑或智能手机购物。

transcript.text: Online spending on Black Friday will rise 15 percent to hit 2.7 billion dollars this year.
transcript.translation: 今年黑色星期五的网上消费将增长百分之十五，达到二十七亿美元。

transcript.text: Cyber Monday spending will increase 12 percent to 3 billion dollars.
transcript.translation: 网络星期一的消费将增长百分之十二，达到三十亿美元。

transcript.text: For many, shopping online was a more comfortable alternative than crowded malls.
transcript.translation: 对许多人来说，网上购物是比拥挤的商场更舒适的选择。

transcript.text: The shift to online shopping has had a big impact on traditional shopping malls.
transcript.translation: 向网上购物的转变对传统购物中心产生了巨大影响。

transcript.text: Since 2010, more than 24 shopping malls have closed and an additional 60 are struggling.
transcript.translation: 自2010年以来，已有超过24家购物中心关闭，另有60家正在苦苦支撑。

transcript.text: However, Fortune says the weakest of the malls have closed; the sector is thriving again.
transcript.translation: 然而，《财富》杂志称，那些最弱的商场已经关闭，这个行业正再次繁荣起来。

transcript.text: The International Council of Shopping Centers said 94.2 percent of malls were full or occupied with shops by the end of 2014.
transcript.translation: 国际购物中心协会表示，到2014年底，百分之九十四点二的购物中心已客满或被店铺占用。

transcript.text: That is the highest level in 27 years.
transcript.translation: 这是27年来的最高水平。

transcript.text: Economist Gus Faucher said lower unemployment and rising wages could give Americans more money to spend.
transcript.translation: 经济学家古斯·福彻表示，失业率下降和工资上涨可能让美国人有更多的钱用于消费。

transcript.text: The average American consumer will spend about 805 dollars on gifts.
transcript.translation: 美国消费者平均将在礼物上花费约805美元。

transcript.text: That's about 630.5 billion dollars between November and December, an increase of 3.7 percent from last year.
transcript.translation: 也就是11月到12月之间约六千三百零五亿美元，比去年增长百分之三点七。

transcript.text: Questions 9 to 12 are based on the passage you have just heard.
transcript.translation: 第9到12题基于你刚刚听到的短文。

transcript.text: Question 9. What is the speaker mainly talking about?
transcript.translation: 第9题。说话者主要在谈论什么？

transcript.text: Question 10. How many people will shop on Cyber Monday?
transcript.translation: 第10题。有多少人将在网络星期一购物？

transcript.text: Question 11. What does Fortune say about traditional shopping malls?
transcript.translation: 第11题。《财富》杂志对传统购物中心有何评价？

transcript.text: Question 12. What is said to account for the increased number of shoppers?
transcript.translation: 第12题。据说是什么导致了购物者数量的增加？

questions.questionText: What is the speaker mainly talking about?

options.label: A
options.text: Marketing strategies.

options.label: B
options.text: Holiday shopping.

options.label: C
options.text: Shopping malls.

options.label: D
options.text: Online stores.

questions.analysis: 短文开篇即点明主题：'America's holiday shopping season starts on Black Friday'，随后全程围绕感恩节、黑色星期五、网络星期一等假日购物展开，介绍人数、消费额与渠道变化，故主题为假日购物，选 B。A 营销策略文中未涉及；C 购物中心和 D 网店都只是论述假日购物时提到的局部内容，不能概括全文。
questions.keySentence: America's holiday shopping season starts on Black Friday, the day after Thanksgiving.

questions.questionText: How many people will shop on Cyber Monday?

options.label: A
options.text: About 50% of holiday shoppers.

options.label: B
options.text: About 20-30% of holiday shoppers.

options.label: C
options.text: About 136 million.

options.label: D
options.text: About 183.8 million.

questions.analysis: 原文明确说 'About 183.8 million people will shop on Cyber Monday'，故选 D。C 的 136 million 是感恩节假期周末的购物人数；B 的 20-30% 指零售商年收入占比；A 的 50% 指网上购物占所有假日购物的比例，均非网络星期一的购物人数。
questions.keySentence: About 183.8 million people will shop on Cyber Monday, the first Monday after Thanksgiving.

questions.questionText: What does Fortune say about traditional shopping malls?

options.label: A
options.text: They have fewer customers.

options.label: B
options.text: They find it hard to survive.

options.label: C
options.text: They are thriving once more.

options.label: D
options.text: They appeal to elderly customers.

questions.analysis: 原文 'Fortune says the weakest of the malls have closed; the sector is thriving again' 表明《财富》认为最弱的商场已关闭，该行业再次繁荣，对应 C 'They are thriving once more'。A、B 描述的是 2010 年以来商场关闭、苦苦支撑的早期困境，处于转折词 However 之前，并非《财富》的结论；D 吸引老年顾客文中从未提及。

transcript.text: Passage 2.
transcript.translation: 第二篇短文。

transcript.text: For years, many of us have relied on antibiotic use to treat various infections.
transcript.translation: 多年来，我们当中许多人都依赖使用抗生素来治疗各种感染。

transcript.text: And the reality is that antibiotics have been responsible for saving millions of lives since penicillin, one of the earliest antibiotics, was first used on a clinical basis 70 years ago.
transcript.translation: 事实上，自从最早的抗生素之一青霉素在70年前首次用于临床以来，抗生素已经挽救了数百万人的生命。

transcript.text: However, today is a new era in which taking antibiotics can cause some very dangerous and potentially life-threatening situations.
transcript.translation: 然而，如今进入了一个新时代，服用抗生素可能会带来一些非常危险、甚至可能危及生命的情况。

transcript.text: In fact, you may have heard about the new superbugs, which are antibiotic-resistant bacteria that have developed as a result of overprescribed antibiotics.
transcript.translation: 事实上，你可能听说过新出现的超级细菌，它们是由于抗生素被过度开处方而产生的耐抗生素细菌。

transcript.text: In the past, health experts warned us that the day would come in which it would become very difficult to provide medical care for even common problems, such as lung infection or severe sore throat.
transcript.translation: 过去，健康专家曾警告我们，总有一天，即使是肺部感染或严重咽喉痛这样常见的问题，提供医疗救治也会变得非常困难。

transcript.text: And apparently that day has come, because seemingly routine operations such as knee replacements are now much more hazardous due to the looming threat of these infections.
transcript.translation: 显然那一天已经到来，因为像膝关节置换这样看似常规的手术，如今因为这些感染日益逼近的威胁而变得危险得多。

transcript.text: The problem has grown into such epidemic proportions that this severe strain of resistant bacteria is being blamed for nearly 700,000 deaths each year throughout the world.
transcript.translation: 这一问题已经发展到流行病般的规模，以至于这种严重的耐药菌株被认为造成了全世界每年近70万人死亡。

transcript.text: And unfortunately, health experts worry that the number will rise to 10 million or more on a yearly basis by 2050.
transcript.translation: 不幸的是，健康专家担心，到2050年这一数字将每年上升到1000万或更多。

transcript.text: With such a large life-threatening epidemic, it is sad to say that only 1.2% of budgetary money for the National Institutes of Health is currently being spent on research to tackle this problem.
transcript.translation: 面对如此巨大的、危及生命的流行病，可悲的是，目前美国国家卫生研究院仅有1.2%的预算资金被用于解决这一问题的研究。

transcript.text: This is a far cry from the funds necessary for a problem of such magnitude.
transcript.translation: 这与如此严重的问题所需要的资金相差甚远。

questions.questionText: What do we learn about the superbugs?

options.label: A

questions.analysis: 短文明确定义 'the new superbugs, which are antibiotic-resistant bacteria that have developed as a result of overprescribed antibiotics'（超级细菌就是因抗生素被过度开处方而产生的耐抗生素细菌），故选 D。A 把 bug 误解为昆虫，错；B 指的是被过度开处方的抗生素，那是超级细菌产生的原因而非其本身；C superbugs 是细菌而非疾病。

options.label: C

questions.analysis: 过度开处方导致耐药细菌出现，专家警告 'it would become very difficult to provide medical care for even common problems, such as lung infection or severe sore throat'，即许多感染已难以治愈，故选 B。A 短文未提抗生素短缺；C 浪费税款无据；D 原文说常规手术变得更 'hazardous'（危险）而非选项里的 'complex'（复杂），且那只是后果之一，B 更准确地概括过度使用的总体结果。
questions.keySentence: In the past, health experts warned us that the day would come in which it would become very difficult to provide medical care for even common problems, such as lung infection or severe sore throat.

options.label: D

transcript.text: Recording 1.
transcript.translation: 录音一。

transcript.text: This is the reason you are here in a university. You are here to be educated. You are here to understand thinking better and to think better yourself.
transcript.translation: 这就是你们身处大学的理由。你们来这里是为了接受教育，来这里是为了更好地理解思考，并让自己思考得更好。

transcript.text: It's not a chance you're going to have throughout your lifetime. For the next few years, you have a chance to focus on thinking.
transcript.translation: 这不是你一生中随时都能拥有的机会。在接下来的几年里，你们有机会专注于思考。

transcript.text: I think about some of the students who took advantage of their opportunities in a university. One of the stories I always like to tell is of a freshman seminar that I had a chance to teach at Harvard when I was president of the university.
transcript.translation: 我会想起一些充分利用了大学机会的学生。我最爱讲的一个故事，是关于我担任哈佛大学校长时有幸教授的一个新生研讨班。

transcript.text: I taught a seminar on globalization and I assigned a reading that I had written about global capital flows. And as I did each week, I asked one of the students to introduce the readings.
transcript.translation: 我教的是一门关于全球化的研讨课，我布置了一篇自己撰写的、关于全球资本流动的阅读材料。和每周一样，我请一位学生来介绍这些阅读材料。

transcript.text: And this young man in October of his freshman year said something like the following. The reading by President Summers on the flow of capital across countries, it was kind of interesting, but the data did not come close to supporting the conclusions.
transcript.translation: 这个年轻人在他大一的十月份说了大致如下的话：萨默斯校长这篇关于跨国资本流动的阅读材料，还算有点意思，但数据远远不足以支撑文中的结论。

transcript.text: And I thought to myself, what a fantastic thing this was. How could somebody who had been there for five weeks tell the person who had the title president that he didn't really know what he was talking about? And it was a special moment.
transcript.translation: 我心想，这真是太棒了。一个才来了五个星期的人，怎么能对一位顶着校长头衔的人说，他其实并不懂自己在讲什么呢？那真是一个特别的时刻。

transcript.text: Now, I don't want to be misunderstood. I explained to my student that I actually thought he was rather more confused than I was. And I argued back.
transcript.translation: 不过，我不想被误解。我向那位学生解释说，我其实觉得他比我更糊涂，于是我也反驳了回去。

transcript.text: But what was really important about that was the universities stand out as places that really are about the authority of ideas. You see it in faculty members who are pleased when their students make a discovery that undermines a cherished theory that they had put forward.
transcript.translation: 但真正重要的是，大学之所以与众不同，正在于它们是崇尚思想权威的地方。你可以在教师身上看到这一点：当学生作出某个发现、推翻了他们曾经珍视并提出的理论时，他们反而感到高兴。

transcript.text: I think of another student I had who came to me one evening, walked into my office and said that I had written a pretty good paper, but that it had five important mistakes and that he wanted a job.
transcript.translation: 我还想起另一位学生，他一天傍晚来找我，走进我的办公室说，我写了一篇相当不错的论文，但里面有五个重要的错误，而且他想要一份工作。

transcript.text: You could debate whether they actually were mistakes, but you couldn't debate that young man's hunger to learn. You could not debate that that young man was someone who wanted to make a difference in economics.
transcript.translation: 你可以争论那些到底算不算错误，但你无法否认那个年轻人对学习的渴望。你无法否认那个年轻人是一个想要在经济学领域有所建树的人。

transcript.text: And he is today a professor of economics, and his works are more cited as an economist than any other economist in the world.
transcript.translation: 如今他已是一位经济学教授，作为经济学家，他的著作被引用的次数超过了世界上任何其他经济学家。

transcript.translation: 第16至18题基于你刚刚听到的录音。

transcript.text: Question 16. What does the speaker say about a university?
transcript.translation: 第16题。说话人谈到大学时说了什么？

transcript.text: Question 17. What do we learn from the speaker's stories about universities?
transcript.translation: 第17题。从说话人讲述的故事中，我们对大学有什么了解？

transcript.text: Question 18. What does the speaker see in the young man who challenged his paper?
transcript.translation: 第18题。说话人在那个质疑他论文的年轻人身上看到了什么？

questions.questionText: What does the speaker say about a university?

options.label: A
options.text: It is accessible only to the talented.

options.label: B
options.text: It improves students’ ability to think.

options.label: C
options.text: It starts a lifelong learning process.

options.label: D
options.text: It gives birth to many eminent scholars.

questions.analysis: 录音开头说话人明确指出来大学的目的：'You are here to understand thinking better and to think better yourself.'（你们来这里是为了更好地理解思考、让自己思考得更好），强调大学提升学生的思考能力，故选 B。A 文中只说这是难得的机会，并未说只对有天赋者开放；C 说话人恰恰说这种专注思考的机会'不是一生中随时都有的'，与'终身学习'相反；D '培养众多杰出学者'是后文举例的附带结果，并非他对大学本质的概括。
questions.keySentence: You are here to understand thinking better and to think better yourself.

questions.questionText: What do we learn from the speaker's stories about universities?

options.label: A
options.text: They encourage academic democracy.

options.label: B
options.text: They promote globalization.

options.label: C
options.text: They uphold the presidents’ authority.

options.label: D
options.text: They protect students’ rights.

questions.analysis: 说话人通过一名新生当面质疑校长论文的故事，得出结论：'universities stand out as places that really are about the authority of ideas'（大学之所以与众不同，正在于崇尚思想的权威而非头衔的权威），即鼓励不论身份的学术平等与争鸣，故选 A。B 全球化只是研讨课的主题，并非故事要说明的道理；C 恰好相反，故事强调的是思想的权威而非校长的权威；D 文中并未谈及保护学生权利。
questions.keySentence: But what was really important about that was the universities stand out as places that really are about the authority of ideas.

questions.questionText: What does the speaker see in the young man who challenged his paper?

options.label: A
options.text: His thirst for knowledge.

options.label: B
options.text: His eagerness to find a job.

options.label: C
options.text: His contempt for authority.

options.label: D
options.text: His potential for leadership.

questions.analysis: 说话人评价那个指出他论文五处错误的学生时说：'you couldn't debate that young man's hunger to learn'（你无法否认那个年轻人对学习的渴望），thirst for knowledge 正是 hunger to learn 的同义改写，故选 A。B 学生虽提到'wanted a job'，但说话人看重的是其求知欲而非找工作的急切；C 学生质疑权威是出于求知而非'蔑视'权威；D 文中提到他后来成为引用率最高的经济学家，体现学术成就而非'领导潜质'。
questions.keySentence: You could debate whether they actually were mistakes, but you couldn't debate that young man's hunger to learn.

transcript.text: Recording 2.
transcript.translation: 录音二。

transcript.text: Psychological research shows we consistently underestimate our mental powers.
transcript.translation: 心理学研究表明，我们总是一贯地低估自己的智力。

transcript.text: If you think this does not apply to you, then here is a simple test to show you are wrong.
transcript.translation: 如果你认为这不适用于你，那么这里有一个简单的测试可以证明你是错的。

transcript.text: Write down the names of all the American states you can remember.
transcript.translation: 写下你所能记住的所有美国州名。

transcript.text: Put the list away and then set yourself the same task a week later.
transcript.translation: 把这份清单收起来，一周后再让自己做同样的任务。

transcript.text: Provided you have not cheated by consulting an atlas, you will notice something rather surprising.
transcript.translation: 只要你没有靠查阅地图册作弊，你就会注意到一些相当令人惊讶的现象。

transcript.text: The two lists will contain roughly the same number of states, but they will not be identical.
transcript.translation: 这两份清单所含的州数大致相同，但它们并不完全一样。

transcript.text: Some names will have slipped away, but others will have replaced them.
transcript.translation: 有些名字会消失，但另一些名字会取而代之。

transcript.text: This suggests that somewhere in your mind you may well have a record of virtually every state.
transcript.translation: 这表明，在你脑海的某个地方，你很可能记录着几乎每一个州。

transcript.text: So it is not really your memory letting you down, just your ability to retrieve information from it.
transcript.translation: 所以真正让你失望的并不是你的记忆力，而只是你从记忆中提取信息的能力。

transcript.text: We would remember a lot more if we had more confidence in our memories and knew how to use them properly.
transcript.translation: 如果我们对自己的记忆更有信心，并且懂得如何正确地使用它们，我们就能记住更多东西。

transcript.text: One useful tip is that things are more likely to be remembered if you are in exactly the same state and place as you were when you learned them.
transcript.translation: 一个有用的窍门是：如果你处于与学习时完全相同的状态和地点，那么事物就更容易被记住。

transcript.text: So if you are a student who always reviews over black coffee, perhaps it would be sensible to prime yourself with a cup before the exam.
transcript.translation: 所以如果你是一个总是边喝黑咖啡边复习的学生，也许在考试前先给自己来上一杯是明智的做法。

transcript.text: If possible, you should also try to learn information in the room where it is going to be tested.
transcript.translation: 如果可能的话，你还应该尽量在将要进行考试的房间里学习相关信息。

transcript.text: When you learn is also important.
transcript.translation: 你在什么时候学习也很重要。

transcript.text: Lots of people swear they can absorb new information more efficiently at some times of the day than at others.
transcript.translation: 很多人坚信，他们在一天中的某些时段比其他时段能更高效地吸收新信息。

transcript.text: Research shows this is not just imagination.
transcript.translation: 研究表明，这并非只是想象。

transcript.text: There is a biological rhythm for learning.
transcript.translation: 学习存在着一种生物节律。

transcript.text: Though it affects different people in different ways, for most of us the best plan is to take in new information in the morning and then try to consolidate it into memory during the afternoon.
transcript.translation: 虽然它对不同的人有不同的影响，但对我们大多数人来说，最好的安排是上午吸收新信息，然后在下午努力把它巩固进记忆中。

transcript.text: But this does not apply to everyone, so it is essential to establish your own rhythm.
transcript.translation: 但这并不适用于每个人，所以确立你自己的节律至关重要。

transcript.text: You can do this by learning a set number of lines of poetry at different times of the day and seeing when most lines stick.
transcript.translation: 你可以通过在一天的不同时段背诵固定数量的诗句，并看看在什么时候记住的诗句最多来做到这一点。

transcript.text: When you have done this, try to organize your life so that the time set aside for learning coincides with the time when your memory is at its best.
transcript.translation: 做完这件事后，尽量安排好你的生活，让留给学习的时间正好与你记忆力最佳的时间相吻合。

transcript.text: Avoid learning marathons. They do not make the best use of your mind.
transcript.translation: 避免马拉松式的学习。它们并不能最好地利用你的大脑。

transcript.text: Take plenty of breaks because they offer a double bonus.
transcript.translation: 多多休息，因为休息能带来双重好处。

transcript.text: The time off gives your mind a chance to do some preliminary consolidation and it also gives a memory boost to the learning.
transcript.translation: 休息时间让你的大脑有机会做一些初步的巩固，同时也对学习起到增强记忆的作用。

transcript.text: Questions 19 to 22 are based on the recording you have just heard.
transcript.translation: 问题19至22基于你刚刚听到的录音。

transcript.text: Question 19. What does the simple test suggest?
transcript.translation: 问题19。这个简单的测试说明了什么？

transcript.text: Question 20. What do we learn about the two lists in the test?
transcript.translation: 问题20。关于测试中的两份清单，我们了解到了什么？

transcript.text: Question 21. What does the speaker suggest about preparing for and taking an exam?
transcript.translation: 问题21。关于备考和参加考试，说话者提出了什么建议？

transcript.text: Question 22. What tip does the speaker give on learning?
transcript.translation: 问题22。说话者给出了关于学习的什么窍门？

questions.questionText: What does the simple test suggest?

options.label: A
options.text: Few people know how to retrieve information properly.

options.label: B
options.text: People can enhance their memory with a few tricks.

options.label: C
options.text: Most people have a rather poor long-term memory.

options.label: D
options.text: People tend to underestimate their mental powers.

questions.analysis: 录音开篇即点明主旨：'Psychological research shows we consistently underestimate our mental powers',紧接着说这个简单测试正是用来证明你低估了自己,故选 D。A 偏离该测试要说明的结论;B 是后文另一观点而非这个测试的核心要旨;C 与录音相反,录音强调记忆其实记录了几乎每个州,问题在于提取而非记忆差。
questions.keySentence: Psychological research shows we consistently underestimate our mental powers. If you think this does not apply to you, then here is a simple test to show you are wrong.

questions.questionText: What do we learn about the two lists in the test?

options.label: A
options.text: They present the states in a surprisingly different order.

options.label: B
options.text: They include more or less the same number of states.

options.label: C
options.text: They are exactly the same as is shown in the atlas.

options.label: D
options.text: They contain names of the most familiar states.

questions.analysis: 录音明确说 'The two lists will contain roughly the same number of states, but they will not be identical',即两份清单州数大致相同但不完全一致,故选 B。A 谈的是顺序,录音并未提顺序问题;C 录音特别强调前提是没有查阅地图册,且两份清单互不相同;D 录音并未说清单只含最熟悉的州。
questions.keySentence: The two lists will contain roughly the same number of states, but they will not be identical.

questions.questionText: What does the speaker suggest about preparing for and taking an exam?

options.label: A
options.text: Focusing on what is likely to be tested.

options.label: B
options.text: Having a good sleep the night before.

options.label: C
options.text: Reviewing your lessons where the exam is to take place.

options.label: D
options.text: Making sensible decisions while choosing your answers.

questions.analysis: 说话者建议:'If possible, you should also try to learn information in the room where it is going to be tested',即尽量在将要考试的房间里复习,与 C '在考试地点复习功课' 一致,故选 C。A、D 录音都没有提及备考要点或答题决策;B 录音谈的是学习节律和休息,并未建议考前睡个好觉。
questions.keySentence: If possible, you should also try to learn information in the room where it is going to be tested.

questions.questionText: What tip does the speaker give on learning?

options.label: A
options.text: Discover when you can learn best.

options.label: B
options.text: Change your time of study daily.

options.label: C
options.text: Give yourself a double bonus afterwards.

options.label: D

transcript.text: Hello. Today I am going to talk about poverty.
transcript.translation: 大家好。今天我要谈谈贫困这个话题。

transcript.text: Poverty has become a critical issue in today's world. It concerns not only us sociologists but also economists, politicians and business people.
transcript.translation: 贫困已成为当今世界一个至关重要的问题。它不仅关系到我们社会学家，也关系到经济学家、政治家和商人。

transcript.text: Poverty has been understood in many different ways. One useful way is to distinguish between three degrees of poverty: extreme poverty, moderate poverty and relative poverty.
transcript.translation: 人们以多种不同的方式理解贫困。一种有用的方式是把贫困区分为三种程度：极端贫困、中度贫困和相对贫困。

transcript.text: The first type of poverty is extreme poverty. It is also called absolute poverty.
transcript.translation: 第一种贫困是极端贫困。它也被称为绝对贫困。

transcript.text: In extreme poverty, households cannot meet basic needs for survival. People are chronically hungry. They are unable to access safe drinking water, let alone health care. They cannot afford education for their children.
transcript.translation: 在极端贫困中，家庭无法满足基本的生存需求。人们长期处于饥饿状态。他们无法获得安全的饮用水，更不用说医疗了。他们负担不起子女的教育。

transcript.text: In short, people who live in extreme poverty do not have even the minimum resources to support themselves and their families.
transcript.translation: 简而言之，生活在极端贫困中的人们甚至连维持自己和家人生计所需的最低限度资源都没有。

transcript.text: Where does extreme poverty occur? Well, you can find it only in developing countries.
transcript.translation: 极端贫困发生在哪里呢？嗯，你只能在发展中国家找到它。

transcript.text: Well, what about moderate poverty? Unlike extreme poverty, moderate poverty generally refers to conditions of life in which basic needs are met but barely.
transcript.translation: 那么中度贫困又如何呢？与极端贫困不同，中度贫困通常指的是基本需求得到满足、但仅仅勉强满足的生活状况。

transcript.text: People living in moderate poverty have the resources to keep themselves alive, but only at a very basic level.
transcript.translation: 生活在中度贫困中的人们拥有维持生命的资源，但仅仅处于非常基本的水平。

transcript.text: For example, they may have access to drinking water but not clean, safe drinking water. They may have a home to shelter themselves, but it does not have power supply, a telephone or plumbing.
transcript.translation: 例如，他们可能有饮用水，但不是干净、安全的饮用水。他们可能有遮风挡雨的住所，但没有电力供应、电话或管道设施。

transcript.text: The third kind of poverty is relative poverty. Relative poverty is generally considered to be a household income level which is below a given proportion of average family income.
transcript.translation: 第三种贫困是相对贫困。相对贫困通常被认为是低于平均家庭收入某一特定比例的家庭收入水平。

transcript.text: The relatively poor live in high-income countries, but they do not have a high income themselves.
transcript.translation: 相对贫困者生活在高收入国家，但他们本身收入并不高。

transcript.text: The method of calculating the poverty line is different from country to country, but we can say that basically a family living in relative poverty has less than a certain percentage of the average family income.
transcript.translation: 计算贫困线的方法因国家而异，但我们可以说，生活在相对贫困中的家庭基本上其收入低于平均家庭收入的某一百分比。

transcript.text: For example, in the United States, a family can be considered poor if their income is less than 50% of the national average family income.
transcript.translation: 例如，在美国，如果一个家庭的收入低于全国平均家庭收入的 50%，就可以被认为是贫困的。

transcript.text: They can meet their basic needs, but they lack access to cultural goods, entertainment and recreation. They also do not have access to quality health care or other prerequisites for upward social mobility.
transcript.translation: 他们能满足基本需求，但缺乏获得文化产品、娱乐和休闲的途径。他们也无法获得优质的医疗服务或其他向上社会流动的必要条件。

transcript.text: Well, I have briefly explained to you how poverty can be distinguished as extreme poverty, moderate poverty and relative poverty.
transcript.translation: 好了，我已经向你们简要解释了如何将贫困区分为极端贫困、中度贫困和相对贫困。

transcript.text: We should keep these distinctions in mind when we research people's living conditions, either in the developing or the developed world.
transcript.translation: 当我们研究人们的生活状况时，无论是在发展中世界还是发达世界，都应该牢记这些区别。

paragraphs.text: Half of your brain stays alert and prepared for danger when you sleep in a new place, a study has revealed. This phenomenon is often __26__ to as the "first-night-effect". Researchers from Brown University found that a network in the left hemisphere of the brain "remained more active" than the network in the right side of the brain. Playing sounds into the right ears (stimulating the left hemisphere) of __27__ was more likely to wake them up than if the noises were played into their left ears.
paragraphs.translation: 一项研究揭示，当你在陌生地方睡觉时，一半的大脑保持警觉并准备应对危险。这种现象通常被称为“首夜效应”。布朗大学的研究人员发现，大脑左半球的一个网络比右半球的网络“保持更活跃”。向志愿者的右耳播放声音（刺激左半球）比向他们的左耳播放噪音更有可能唤醒他们。

paragraphs.text: It was __28__ observed that the left side of the brain was more active during deep sleep. When the researchers repeated the laboratory experiment on the second and third nights they found the left hemisphere could not be stimulated in the same way during deep sleep. The researchers explained that the study demonstrated when we are in a __29__ environment the brain partly remains alert so that humans can defend themselves against any __30__ danger.
paragraphs.translation: 特别观察到，在深度睡眠期间，大脑的左侧更为活跃。当研究人员在第二和第三个晚上重复实验室实验时，他们发现左半球在深度睡眠期间无法以相同方式被刺激。研究人员解释说，这项研究表明，当我们处于新环境时，大脑部分保持警觉，以便人类能够抵御任何潜在危险。

paragraphs.text: The researchers believe this is the first time that the "first-night-effect" of different brain states has been __31__ in humans. It isn't, however, the first time it has ever been seen. Some animals __32__ also display this phenomenon. For example, dolphins, as well as other __33__ animals, shut down one hemisphere of the brain when they go to sleep. A previous study noted that dolphins always __34__ control their breathing. Without keeping the brain active while sleeping, they would probably drown. But, as the human study suggests, another reason for dolphins keeping their eyes open during sleep is that they can look out for __35__ while asleep. It also keeps their physiological processes working.
paragraphs.translation: 研究人员认为，这是首次在人类中识别出不同脑状态的“首夜效应”。然而，这并不是首次观察到这种现象。一些动物物种也表现出这种现象。例如，海豚以及其他海洋动物在睡觉时会关闭大脑的一个半球。一项先前的研究指出，海豚总是谨慎控制它们的呼吸。如果在睡眠中不保持大脑活跃，它们很可能会淹死。但是，正如人类研究所表明的，海豚在睡眠中保持眼睛睁开的另一个原因是它们可以在睡觉时警惕捕食者。这也保持它们的生理过程正常运作。

questionGroups.title: Elite Math Competitions Struggle to Diversify Their Talent Pool

material.title: Elite Math Competitions Struggle to Diversify Their Talent Pool

paragraphs.text: Interest in elite high school math competitions has grown in recent years, and in light of last summer's U.S. win at the International Math Olympiad (IMO)-the first for an American team in more than two decades-the trend is likely to continue.
paragraphs.translation: 近年来，精英高中数学竞赛的兴趣日益增长，鉴于去年夏天美国在国际数学奥林匹克竞赛（IMO）中获胜——这是美国队二十多年来的首次——这一趋势可能会持续。

paragraphs.text: But will such contests, which are overwhelmingly dominated by Asian and white students from middle- class and affluent families, become any more diverse? Many social and cultural factors play roles in determining which promising students get on the path toward international math recognition. But efforts are in place to expose more black, Hispanic, and low-income students to advanced math, in the hope that the demographic pool of high-level contenders will eventually begin to shift and become less exclusive.
paragraphs.translation: 但是，这些竞赛主要由来自中产阶级和富裕家庭的亚裔和白人学生主导，它们会变得更加多元化吗？许多社会和文化因素决定了哪些有潜力的学生能够踏上国际数学认可的道路。但已有努力正在实施，以让更多黑人、西班牙裔和低收入学生接触高等数学，希望高级别竞争者的群体构成最终开始转变，变得不那么排他。

paragraphs.text: "The challenge is if certain types of people are doing something, it's difficult for other people to break into it," said Po-Shen Loh, the head coach of last year's winning U.S. Math Olympiad team. Participation grows through friends and networks and if "you realize that's how they're growing, you can start to take action" and bring in other students, he said.
paragraphs.translation: "挑战在于，如果某些类型的人在做某事，其他人就很难打入其中，"去年获胜的美国数学奥林匹克队主教练罗博深说。参与度通过朋友和网络增长，如果你意识到"那就是他们如何增长的，你可以开始采取行动"并引入其他学生，他说。

paragraphs.text: Most of the training for advanced-math competitions happens outside the confines of the normal school day. Students attend after-school clubs, summer camps, online forums and classes, and university-based "math circles," to prepare for the competitions.
paragraphs.translation: 高等数学竞赛的大部分训练发生在正常学校日之外。学生参加课外俱乐部、夏令营、在线论坛和课程，以及大学的"数学圈"，来准备竞赛。

paragraphs.text: One of the largest feeders for high school math competitions — including those that eventually lead to the IMO— is a middle school program called MathCounts. About 100,000 students around the country participate in the program's competition series, which culminates in a national game-show-style contest held each May. The most recent one took place last week in Washington, D.C. Students join a team through their schools, which provide a volunteer coach and pay a nominal fee to send students to regional and state competitions. The 224 students who make it to the national competition get an all-expenses-paid trip.
paragraphs.translation: 高中数学竞赛最大的来源之一——包括最终通向IMO的竞赛——是一个名为MathCounts的中学项目。全国约有10万名学生参与该项目的竞赛系列，最终在每年五月举行全国性的游戏节目式竞赛。最近的一次于上周在华盛顿特区举行。学生通过学校加入团队，学校提供志愿教练并支付象征性费用送学生参加地区和州级竞赛。进入全国竞赛的224名学生获得全额资助的旅行。

paragraphs.text: Nearly all members of last year's winning U.S. IMO team took part in MathCounts as middle school students, as did Loh, the coach. "Middle school is an important age because students have enough math capability to solve advanced problems, but they haven't really decided what they want to do with their lives," said Loh. "They often get hooked then."
paragraphs.translation: 去年获胜的美国IMO队的几乎所有成员都曾在中学时期参与MathCounts，教练罗博深也是如此。"中学是一个重要的年龄，因为学生有足够的数学能力解决高级问题，但他们还没有真正决定他们想做什么，"罗博深说。"他们通常在那时上瘾。"

paragraphs.text: Another influential feeder for advanced-math students is an online school called Art of Problem Solving, which began about 13 years ago and now has 15,000 users. Students use forums to chat, play games, and solve problems together at no cost, or they can pay a few hundred dollars to take courses with trained teachers. According to Richard Rusczyk, the company founder, the six U.S. team members who competed at the IMO last year collectively took more than 40 courses on the site. Parents of advanced-math students and MathCounts coaches say the children are on the website constantly.
paragraphs.translation: 高等数学学生的另一个有影响力的来源是一所名为"问题解决艺术"的在线学校，它始于大约13年前，现在有15,000名用户。学生可以免费使用论坛聊天、玩游戏和一起解决问题，或者他们可以支付几百美元接受训练有素的教师课程。根据公司创始人理查德·鲁斯克的说法，去年参加IMO的六名美国队成员在网站上总共修了40多门课程。高等数学学生的家长和MathCounts教练说孩子们经常上这个网站。

paragraphs.text: There are also dozens of summer camps―many attached to universities — that aim to prepare elite math students. Some are pricey—a three-week intensive program can cost $4,500 or more— but most offer scholarships. The Math Olympiad Summer Training Program is a three-week math camp held by the Mathematical Association of America that leads straight to the international championship and is free for those who make it. Only about 50 students are invited based on their performance on written tests and at the USA Math Olympiad.
paragraphs.translation: 还有数十个夏令营——许多附属于大学——旨在培养精英数学学生。有些价格昂贵——一个为期三周的强化课程可能花费4,500美元或更多——但大多数提供奖学金。数学奥林匹克暑期培训项目是由美国数学协会举办的为期三周的数学营，直接通向国际锦标赛，对于入选者免费。只有约50名学生基于他们在笔试和美国数学奥林匹克中的表现被邀请。

paragraphs.text: Students in university towns may also have access to another lever for involvement in accelerated math: math circles. In these groups, which came out of an Eastern European tradition of developing young talent, professors teach promising K-12 students advanced mathematics for several hours after school or on weekends. The Los Angeles Math Circle, held at the University of California, Los Angeles, began in 2007 with 20 students and now has more than 250. "These math circles cost nothing, or they're very cheap for students to get involved in, but you have to know about them," said Rusczyk. "Most people would love to get students from more underserved populations, but they just can't get them in the door. Part of it is communication; part of it is transportation."
paragraphs.translation: 大学城的学生也可能有另一个途径参与加速数学：数学圈。这些团体源于东欧培养年轻人才的传统，教授在课后或周末为有潜力的K-12学生教授高等数学几小时。在加州大学洛杉矶分校举行的洛杉矶数学圈始于2007年，最初有20名学生，现在有超过250名。"这些数学圈免费，或者对学生来说参与成本很低，但你必须知道它们的存在，"鲁斯克说。"大多数人愿意从服务不足的人群中招收学生，但他们就是无法让他们进来。部分原因是沟通；部分原因是交通。"

paragraphs.text: It's no secret in the advanced-math community that diversity is a problem. According to Mark Saul, the director of competitions for the Mathematical Association of America, not a single African-American or Hispanic student— and only a handful of girls― has ever made it to the Math Olympiad team in its 50 years of existence. Many schools simply don't prioritize academic competitions." Do you know who we have to beat?" asked Saul. "The football team, the basketball team — that's our competition for resources, student time, attention, school dollars, parent efforts, school enthusiasm."
paragraphs.translation: 在高等数学社区，多样性是一个问题不是秘密。根据美国数学协会竞赛总监马克·索尔的说法，在其50年的存在中，没有一个非裔或西班牙裔学生——只有少数女孩——曾进入数学奥林匹克队。许多学校根本不优先考虑学术竞赛。"你知道我们必须打败谁吗？"索尔问道。"足球队、篮球队——那是我们争夺资源、学生时间、注意力、学校资金、家长努力、学校热情的竞争对手。"

paragraphs.text: Teachers in low-income urban and rural areas with no history of participating in math competitions may not know about advanced-math opportunities like MathCounts—and those who do may not have support or feel trained to lead them.
paragraphs.translation: 在低收入城市和农村地区，没有参与数学竞赛历史的教师可能不知道像MathCounts这样的高等数学机会——而那些知道的人可能没有支持或感觉没有受过训练来领导它们。

paragraphs.text: But there are initiatives in place to try to get more underrepresented students involved in accelerated math. A New York City-based nonprofit called Bridge to Enter Mathematics runs a residential summer program aimed at getting underserved students, mostly black and Hispanic, working toward math and science careers. The summer after 7th grade, students spend three weeks on a college campus studying advanced math for seven hours a day. Over the next five years, the group helps the students get into other elite summer math programs, high-performing high schools, and eventually college. About 250 students so far have gone through the program, which receives funding from the Jack Kent Cooke Foundation.
paragraphs.translation: 但有一些倡议正在实施，试图让更多代表不足的学生参与加速数学。一个名为"桥接进入数学"的纽约市非营利组织运营一个住宿夏令营项目，旨在让服务不足的学生——主要是黑人和西班牙裔——朝着数学和科学职业努力。七年级后的夏天，学生在大学校园里度过三周，每天学习高等数学七小时。在接下来的五年里，该组织帮助学生进入其他精英暑期数学项目、高性能高中，最终进入大学。迄今为止，约有250名学生参加了该项目，该项目由杰克·肯特·库克基金会资助。

paragraphs.text: "If you look at a lot of low-income communities in the United States, there are programs that are serving them, but they're primarily centered around 'Let's get these kids' grades up,' and not around 'let's get these kids access to the same kinds of opportunities as more-affluent kids,'" said Daniel Zaharopol, the founder and executive director of the program. "We're trying to create that pathway." Students apply to the program directly through their schools."We want to reach parents who are not plugged into the system," said Zaharopol.
paragraphs.translation: "如果你看美国很多低收入社区，有服务于他们的项目，但这些项目主要围绕'让我们提高这些孩子的成绩'，而不是'让这些孩子获得与更富裕孩子相同的机会，'"该项目的创始人兼执行董事丹尼尔·扎哈罗波尔说。"我们正试图创造那条途径。"学生直接通过学校申请该项目。"我们希望接触到没有融入系统的家长，"扎哈罗波尔说。

paragraphs.text: In the past few years, MathCounts added two new middle school programs to try to diversify its participant pool — the National Math Club and the Math Video Challenge. Schools or teachers who sign up for the National Math Club receive a kit full of activities and resources, but there's no special teacher training and no competition attached.
paragraphs.translation: 在过去几年里，MathCounts增加了两个新的中学项目，以试图多样化其参与者池——全国数学俱乐部和数学视频挑战赛。注册全国数学俱乐部的学校或教师会收到一个装满活动和资源的工具包，但没有特殊的教师培训，也没有附加竞赛。

paragraphs.text: The Math Video Challenge is a competition, but a collaborative one. Teams of four students make a video illustrating a math problem and its real-world application. After the high-pressure Countdown round at this year's national MathCounts competition, in which the top 12 students went head to head solving complex problems in rapid fire, the finalists for the Math Video Challenge took the stage to show their videos. The demographics of that group looked quite different from those in the competition round of the 16 video finalists, 13 were girls and eight were African-American students. The video challenge does not put individual students on the hot seat — so it's less intimidating by design. It also adds the element of artistic creativity to attract a new pool of students who may not see themselves as "math people."
paragraphs.translation: 数学视频挑战赛是一个竞赛，但一个协作性的。四名学生组成的团队制作一个视频，阐述一个数学问题及其现实应用。在今年全国MathCounts竞赛的高压倒计时轮之后，其中前12名学生一对一快速解决复杂问题，数学视频挑战赛的决赛选手上台展示他们的视频。该群体的人口统计与竞赛轮中的16名视频决赛选手相比大不相同，其中13名是女孩，8名是非裔美国学生。视频挑战赛不把个别学生放在热点上——所以它在设计上不那么令人畏惧。它还加入了艺术创造力的元素，以吸引可能不自视为"数学人"的新学生池。

questionGroups.title: Passage One

paragraphs.text: We live today indebted to McCardell, Cashin, Hawes, Wilkins, and Maxwell, and other women who liberated American fashion from the confines of Parisian design. Independence came in tying, wrapping, storing, harmonizing, and rationalizing that wardrobe. These designers established the modern dress code, letting play suits and other active wear outfits suffice for casual clothing, allowing pants to enter the wardrobe, and prizing rationalism and versatility in dress, in contradiction to dressing for an occasion or allotment of the day. Fashion in America was logical and answerable to the will of the women who wore it. Implicitly or explicitly, American fashion addressed a democracy, whereas traditional Paris-based fashion was prescriptive and imposed on women, willing or not.
paragraphs.translation: 今天，我们感激McCardell、Cashin、Hawes、Wilkins和Maxwell以及其他女性，她们将美国时尚从巴黎设计的束缚中解放出来。独立体现在系扎、包裹、储存、协调和合理化衣橱方面。这些设计师建立了现代着装规范，让休闲套装和其他运动服装足以作为日常服装，允许裤子进入衣橱，并推崇着装中的理性主义和多功能性，这与为特定场合或一天中不同时段而着装的做法相矛盾。美国时尚是合乎逻辑的，并响应穿着它的女性的意愿。无论是隐含的还是明确的，美国时尚体现了一种民主，而传统的基于巴黎的时尚是规范性的，强加给女性，无论她们愿意与否。

paragraphs.text: In an earlier time, American fashion had also followed the dictates of Paris, or even copied and pirated specific French designs. Designer sportswear was not modeled on that of Europe, as "modern art" would later be; it was genuinely invented and developed in America. Its designers were not high-end with supplementary lines. The design objective and the business commitment were to sportswear, and the distinctive traits were problem-solving ingenuity and realistic lifestyle applications. Ease of care was most important: summer dresses and outfits, in particular, were chiefly cotton, readily capable of being washed and pressed at home. Closings were simple, practical, and accessible, as the modern woman depended on no personal maid to dress her. American designers prized resourcefulness and the freedom of women who wore the clothing.
paragraphs.translation: 在更早的时候，美国时尚也曾遵循巴黎的指令，甚至抄袭和盗用具体的法国设计。设计师运动服装并非模仿欧洲的，就像“现代艺术”后来那样；它是在美国真正发明和发展的。其设计师并非高端且有附加产品线。设计目标和商业承诺都专注于运动服装，其独特特点是解决问题的创造力和现实生活方式的应用。易于护理最为重要：特别是夏装和套装，主要是棉质，便于在家洗涤和熨烫。闭合方式简单、实用且易得，因为现代女性不依赖个人女仆为她着装。美国设计师推崇机智和穿着服装的女性的自由。

paragraphs.text: Many have argued that the women designers of this time were able to project their own clothing values into a new style. Of course, much of this argument in the 1930s-40s was advanced because there was little or no experience in justifying (证明) on the basis of utility. If Paris was cast aside, the tradition of beauty was also to some degree slighted. Designer sportswear would have to be verified by a standard other than that of pure beauty; the emulation of a designer's life in designer sportswear was a crude version of this relationship. The consumer was ultimately to be mentioned as well, especially by the likes of Dorothy Shaver, who could point to the sales figures at Lord & Taylor.
paragraphs.translation: 许多人认为，这个时代的女性设计师能够将自己的服装价值观投射到新风格中。当然，在20世纪30-40年代，这一观点的提出很大程度上是因为几乎或完全没有基于实用性来证明（证明）的经验。如果巴黎被摒弃，美的传统也在一定程度上被轻视。设计师运动服装必须通过纯美标准以外的标准来验证；在设计师运动服装中模仿设计师的生活是这种关系的粗糙版本。消费者最终也需要被提及，尤其是像Dorothy Shaver这样的人，她可以指出Lord & Taylor的销售数据。

paragraphs.text: Could utility alone justify the new ideas of the American designers? Fashion is often regarded as a pursuit of beauty, and some cherished fashion's trivial relationship to the fine arts. What the designers of American sportswear proved was that fashion is a genuine design art, answering to the demanding needs of service. Of course these practical, insightful designers have determined the course of late twentieth-century fashion. They were the pioneers of gender equity, in their useful, adaptable clothing, which was both made for the masses and capable of self-expression.
paragraphs.translation: 仅凭实用性就能证明美国设计师的新理念吗？时尚常被视为对美的追求，有些人珍视时尚与美术的琐碎关系。美国运动服装设计师所证明的是，时尚是一种真正的设计艺术，回应服务的苛刻需求。当然，这些务实、富有洞察力的设计师决定了20世纪后期时尚的进程。他们是性别平等的先驱，其服装实用、适应性强，既为大众设计，又能实现自我表达。

questionGroups.title: Passage Two

paragraphs.text: Massive rubbish dumps and sprawling landfills constitute one of the more uncomfortable impacts that humans have on wildlife. They have led some birds to give up on migration. Instead of flying thousands of miles in search of food, they make the waste sites their winter feeding grounds.
paragraphs.translation: 大规模垃圾堆和蔓延的垃圾填埋场构成了人类对野生动物更令人不安的影响之一。它们已导致一些鸟类放弃迁徙。这些鸟类不再飞行数千英里寻找食物，而是将废物站点作为它们的冬季觅食地。

paragraphs.text: Researchers in Germany used miniature GPS tags to track the migrations of 70 white storks from different sites across Europe and Asia during the first five months of their lives. While many birds travelled along well-known routes to warmer climates, others stopped short and spent the winter on landfills, feeding on food waste, and the multitudes of insects that thrive on the dumps.
paragraphs.translation: 德国的研究人员使用微型GPS标签追踪了70只白鹳在生命头五个月从欧洲和亚洲不同地点的迁徙。虽然许多鸟类沿着已知路线飞往更温暖的气候区，但其他鸟类中途停止，在垃圾填埋场过冬，以食物残渣和大量滋生在垃圾堆上的昆虫为食。

paragraphs.text: In the short-term, the birds seem to benefit from overwintering (过冬) on rubbish dumps. Andrea Flack of the Max Planck Institute found that birds following traditional migration routes were more likely to die than German storks that flew only as far as northern Morocco, and spent the winter there on rubbish dumps. "For the birds it's a very convenient way to get food. There are huge clusters of organic waste they can feed on," said Flack. The meals are not particularly appetising, or even safe. Much of the waste is discarded rotten meat, mixed in with other human debris such as plastic bags and old toys.
paragraphs.translation: 短期内，鸟类似乎从在垃圾堆上过冬中受益。马克斯·普朗克研究所的安德烈亚·弗拉克发现，遵循传统迁徙路线的鸟类比那些只飞到北非摩洛哥并在那里垃圾堆过冬的德国白鹳更有可能死亡。弗拉克说：“对鸟类来说，这是一种获取食物的便捷方式。有大量有机废物可供它们取食。”这些食物并不特别开胃，甚至不安全。大部分废物是丢弃的腐肉，混杂着其他人类残余物，如塑料袋和旧玩具。

paragraphs.text: "It's very risky. The birds can easily eat pieces of plastic or rubber bands and they can die," said Flack. "And we don't know about the long-term consequences. They might eat something toxic and damage their health. We cannot estimate that yet."
paragraphs.translation: 弗拉克说：“这非常危险。鸟类很容易吃下塑料片或橡皮筋，它们可能会死亡。而且我们不知道长期后果。它们可能吃下有毒物质，损害健康。我们目前还无法估计。”

paragraphs.text: The scientists tracked white storks from different colonies in Europe and Africa. The Russian, Greek and Polish storks flew as far as South Africa, while those from Spain, Tunisia and Germany flew only as far as the Sahel.
paragraphs.translation: 科学家追踪了来自欧洲和非洲不同群体的白鹳。俄罗斯、希腊和波兰的白鹳飞到了南非，而来自西班牙、突尼斯和德国的白鹳只飞到了萨赫勒地区。

paragraphs.text: Landfill sites on the Iberian peninsula have long attracted local white storks, but all of the Spanish birds tagged in the study flew across the Sahara desert to the western Sahel. Writing in the journal, the scientists describe how the storks from Germany were clearly affected by the presence of waste sites, with four out of six birds that survived for at least five months overwintering on rubbish dumps in northern Morocco, instead of migrating to the Sahel.
paragraphs.translation: 伊比利亚半岛的垃圾填埋场长期以来吸引了当地的白鹳，但该研究中所有被标记的西班牙白鹳都飞越撒哈拉沙漠到了萨赫勒西部。科学家在期刊中写道，来自德国的白鹳明显受到废物站点存在的影响，六只中至少存活五个月的四只白鹳在北非摩洛哥的垃圾堆过冬，而不是迁徙到萨赫勒地区。

paragraphs.text: Flack said it was too early to know whether the benefits of plentiful food outweighed the risks of feeding on landfills. But that's not the only uncertainty. Migrating birds affect ecosystems both at home and at their winter destinations, and disrupting the traditional routes could have unexpected side effects. White storks feed on (螳虫) and other insects that can become pests if their numbers get out of hand. "They provide a useful service," said Flack.
paragraphs.translation: 弗拉克说，现在还为时过早，无法知道丰富食物的好处是否超过了在垃圾填埋场觅食的风险。但这并不是唯一的不确定性。迁徙鸟类影响着家乡和冬季目的地的生态系统，扰乱传统路线可能产生意想不到的副作用。白鹳以（蝗虫）和其他昆虫为食，如果这些昆虫数量失控，它们可能会成为害虫。弗拉克说：“它们提供了一种有用的服务。”

questionGroups.directions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.questionText: What is the impact of rubbish dumps on wildlife?

options.label: A
options.text: They have forced white storks to search for safer winter shelters.

options.label: B
options.text: They have seriously polluted the places where birds spend winter.

options.label: C
options.text: They have accelerated the reproduction of some harmful insects.

options.label: D
options.text: They have changed the previous migration habits of certain birds.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。文章第一段提到，rubbish dumps have led some birds to give up on migration，说明垃圾场改变了某些鸟类的迁徙习惯。因此D选项是正确答案。

wrongOptions.A: 原文没有提到white storks被迫寻找更安全的越冬庇护所，A选项属于无中生有。
wrongOptions.B: 虽然垃圾场对环境有污染，但B选项中'seriously polluted'程度过重，原文没有明确提及。
wrongOptions.C: 文章提到rubbish dumps上insects thrive，但并没有说这些昆虫是'harmful insects'，也没有说它们繁殖加速，C选项过度推断。

questions.questionText: What do we learn about birds following the traditional migration routes?

options.label: A
options.text: They can multiply at an accelerating rate.

options.label: B
options.text: They can better pull through the winter.

options.label: C
options.text: They help humans kill harmful insects.

options.label: D
options.text: They are more likely to be at risk of dying.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。文章第四段提到，birds following traditional migration routes were more likely to die than German storks that flew only as far as northern Morocco，说明按照传统迁徙路线飞行的鸟类死亡风险更高。因此D选项是正确答案。

wrongOptions.A: A选项中'multiply at an accelerating rate'与原文信息不符，原文讨论的是死亡率而非繁殖速度。
wrongOptions.B: B选项与原文信息相反，原文说传统迁徙路线的鸟类更可能死亡。
wrongOptions.C: C选项中'help humans kill harmful insects'在原文中未提及，属于无中生有。

questions.questionText: What does Andrea Flack say about the birds overwintering on rubbish dumps?

options.label: A
options.text: They may end up staying there permanently.

options.label: B
options.text: They may eat something harmful.

options.label: C
options.text: They may evolve new feeding habits.

options.label: D
options.text: They may have trouble getting adequate food.

questions.analysis: 这是一道细节理解题。文章倒数第二段提到，'It's very risky. The birds can easily eat pieces of plastic or rubber bands and they can die,' said Flack. 'And we don't know about the long-term consequences. They might eat something toxic and damage their health.' 说明Flack认为在垃圾场上过冬的鸟类可能会吃到有害物质。因此B选项是正确答案。

wrongOptions.A: A选项中'end up staying there permanently'在原文中没有提及，属于过度推断。
wrongOptions.C: C选项中'evolve new feeding habits'在原文中没有提及，属于无中生有。
wrongOptions.D: D选项与原文信息相反，原文说rubbish dumps上有大量有机废物可供食用，不会食物不足。

questions.questionText: What can be inferred about the Spanish birds tagged in the study?

options.label: A
options.text: They gradually lose the habit of migrating in winter.

options.label: B
options.text: They prefer rubbish dumps far away to those at home.

options.label: C
options.text: They are not attracted to the rubbish dumps on their migration routes.

options.label: D
options.text: They join the storks from Germany on rubbish dumps in Morocco.

questions.analysis: 这是一道推理判断题。文章最后一段提到，'Landfill sites on the Iberian peninsula have long attracted local white storks, but all of the Spanish birds tagged in the study flew across the Sahara desert to the western Sahel.' 说明参与研究的西班牙鸟类没有被家门口的垃圾场吸引，而是飞越撒哈拉沙漠去了西非萨赫勒地区。因此C选项是正确答案。

wrongOptions.A: A选项中'gradually lose the habit'在原文中没有提及，属于过度推断。
wrongOptions.B: B选项与原文信息相反，原文说西班牙鸟类没有选择家门口的垃圾场。
wrongOptions.D: D选项中'join the storks from Germany on rubbish dumps in Morocco'在原文中没有提及，属于无中生有。

questions.questionText: What is scientists' other concern about white storks feeding on landfills?

options.label: A
options.text: The potential harm to the ecosystem.

options.label: B
options.text: The genetic change in the stork species.

options.label: C
options.text: The spread of epidemics to their homeland.

options.label: D
options.text: The damaging effect on bio-diversity.

questions.analysis: 这是一道推理判断题。文章最后一段提到，'Migrating birds affect ecosystems both at home and at their winter destinations, and disrupting the traditional routes could have unexpected side effects.' 说明科学家担心迁徙鸟类对生态系统有影响，改变传统迁徙路线可能会带来意外的后果。因此A选项是正确答案。

wrongOptions.B: B选项中'genetic change in the stork species'在原文中没有提及，属于无中生有。
wrongOptions.C: C选项中'spread of epidemics to their homeland'在原文中没有提及，属于无中生有。
wrongOptions.D: D选项中'damaging effect on bio-diversity'虽然与生态系统有关，但原文中没有明确提及生物多样性受损，属于过度推断。

questionGroups.sourceText: 唐朝始于 618 年，终于 907 年，是中国历史上最灿烂的时期。经过近三百年的发展，唐代中国成为世界上最繁荣的强国，其首都长安是当时世界上最大的都市。这一时期，经济发达、商业繁荣、社会秩序稳定，甚至边境也对外开放。随着城市化和财富的增加，艺术和文学也繁荣起来。李白和杜甫是以作品简洁自然而著称的诗人。他们的诗歌打动了学者和普通人的心。即使在今天，他们的许多诗歌仍广为儿童及成人阅读背诵。

answer.modelTranslation: The Tang Dynasty began in 618 and ended in 907, marking the most splendid period in Chinese history. After nearly three hundred years of development, Tang China became the most prosperous and powerful nation in the world, with its capital Chang'an being the largest city at that time. During this period, the economy flourished, commerce thrived, social order was stable, and even the borders were open to the outside world. With urbanization and the increase of wealth, arts and literature also prospered. Li Bai and Du Fu were poets renowned for the simplicity and naturalness of their works. Their poetry touched the hearts of scholars and common people alike. Even today, many of their poems are widely read and recited by children and adults.
